title: The General's Toast
location: Army Day Gala — Officers' Mess, Ashenmere

narrative.text: The Army Day Gala is a sea of pressed uniforms and medals. You stand at the head of the table. General Brenner rises, raises his glass, and the room falls silent. The cameras are flashing.
I raise my glass to the Republic. And I raise my glass to the patience of the military. May the Republic never test that patience too severely.
He didn't toast the Chancellor. He toasted the 'patience of the military.' It's a veiled threat. A public warning. The cameras caught it. You have to respond, and the whole officer corps is watching.

He did it. He looked me in the eye and told the army to be patient with me. It's a dare. If I back down, I look weak. If I lash out, I provoke the very coup he is hinting at. I have to choose my words like a surgeon.

choices.text: Toast back: 'And to the obedience of the military. May it never waver.'
Laugh it off as a joke. Defuse the tension.
Publicly fire him on the spot. 'Your patience is no longer required, General.'
